| [SYNTHESIS-009](../../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-009.md) v2 | Capacity records bound reserve readiness | [QUESTION-395](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-395.md) asks which observations tell a warranted reserve of specialized capability from wasteful redundancy, and which of them identify readiness ([TERM-115](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-115.md)) and which only bound it. [CLAIM-587](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-587.md) makes a response the conjunction of complementary capacities. So records kept per capacity (rosters, training assessments, equipment availability, turnout times) fix only the marginals, which bound readiness by the Fréchet inequalities and do not identify it. A record can refute a required readiness through the weakest capacity, and can certify it only when the shortfalls sum within the margin; between those, only joint evidence decides. With [CLAIM-558](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md)'s decay, a certification expires with the record's age and a refutation does not. The inference leans mainly on [CLAIM-587](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-587.md); its integrating work is joining it with [TERM-115](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-115.md), [CASE-210](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-210.md)'s list of evidence and [CLAIM-558](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md) to answer the question's "identify or bound" half. | [SYNTHESIS-010](../../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-010.md) v2 | When transient support can be withdrawn safely | The assistant's, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to characterize "what differentiates transient support that induces dependency and is hazardous to remove from transient support that builds new capabilities and is safe to remove", with reintroduction and ecological recovery proposed as cases. It draws together the branch's three domains: DNA origami, aid and development, and ecology. Three conditions decide it. First, the support starts a self-sustaining process on an ambient flux instead of doing the upkeep. Planted tree islands, weeded for 2.5 years, kept their advantage to 16–18 years because established trees keep drawing seed dispersers (Holl et al.; Schubert et al.). Supplied repair, by contrast, never becomes optional ([CLAIM-597](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md)). Second, the threat it stood in for is gone. Conservation-reliant species stay reliant while fire is suppressed or habitat threats persist (Mussmann et al.; Brown et al.). Third, the party did the work throughout. Support that does the work wears capacity down by disuse ([CLAIM-558](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md)), by slack effort (Ostrom et al.) or by selection for the supported conditions, which costs hatchery steelhead fitness in the wild within one generation (Christie et al.). Captive-bred translocated stock shows negative population growth (Morris et al.). Persistence must be shown after withdrawal: impact at exit and judged success both overstate it. Revised the same day after two counterpoints the owner asked for. Evidence against the lazy-poor stereotype finds no slack effort in poor households: cash transfers barely change work, and one-off graduation packages raise it. So that route is confined to help that is assured and permanent. A household asset threshold (Balboni et al.) adds a condition on size: support too small decays with no dependence at all. Urban development adds three cautions. Some public inputs are a standing part of a coproduced service (Evans; Watson). Forty years of persistence can be slow reversion (Kline and Moretti). And a place can last while the people it served are dispersed (Collins and Shester; LaVoice). The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. Moved into the SYNTHESIS scheme on 2026-11-07 ([ADR-077](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-077.md)), keeping the standing the status review of 2026-11-06 gave it under the rulings the owner delegated. | Superseded — by [CLAIM-600](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md) |
